🚨Anthropic KYC门槛升级｜Claude现在需要两份政府身份证件才能完成核验

现在Claude的身份验证规则更新：

不能只凭护照即可完成KYC，系统要求从护照、驾照、国民身份证件三者中，提交两类证件。

如果地区选择中国，即便上传护照通过初审，后续还会追加要求补充第二份证件；

但驾照、国民ID两个选项点入后，直接提示该地区不支持身份核验。

简单来说：只拿护照，现在走不通Claude的KYC流程。

text:
wow, amazing technical blog post about microsoft's new 3T pre-training with very rare and clear insights on how to train models of this size

first let's get an overview of the shape of this model, it's a sparser model than Kimi K3 (80B active vs 104B), same sliding window hybrid pattern, with this time more kv heads for the sliding window layers (a bit different from stepfun and poolside that add query head). they added a shared expert and also removed the interleaved MoE/Dense pattern of MAI 1

the scaling ladder is very similar to MAI 1 with the same mechanism, each rung depends only on the number of layers. they mention that one of the key improvements is how they handle the smaller rung data distribution where they make sure to have the same repetition as the final corpus. they already did that for MAI-1 but only for data ablation iirc

their prediction is almost identical to the final run loss, very impressive

they compare the model with different base models such as deepseek v4 pro and MAI 1, tho in the case of deepseek v4 pro i'd say it's quite hard to distinguish how much the data mixture "overfitting" to the scaling ladder has an impact here (they mention it's both), need to always be a bit careful about EG metrics for data in general

they have VERY NICE scaling laws for weight decay and learning rate, for the learning rate they express it as a function of tokens per parameter (N/D) and steps (hence depending on the batch size). they also do the same for dropout where it's a function of active params only, they also find the usual sqrt(k) scaling for learning rate and batch size (other scaling laws often also converge to that)

a bunch of other stability stuff, they use Muon this time and activation gradient clipping, the efficiency gain here is actually pretty crazy at larger scale. they also increase the training horizon to ~40T text (20T unique) + a new 10T (4.5T unique) multimodal  since the model is natively multimodal

imo this is a safe but very clean scaling! very exciting for the tech report and MAI-base-3, congrats!!

text:
不想吃 beta

我们团队的主业是做市和中性策略。

但其实我们手里也有 beta 策略，跑得挺好。曲线漂亮，回撤也在预期里，按收益看，其实很不错的。

最近团队讨论了很久，最后还是决定，不吃这份 beta。

先说清楚 beta 是什么。
beta 是跟着市场赚的钱。

它的收益和市场绑在一起，这对需要方向敞口的人是优点，对我们是负担。它会占用资金和风控额度，会让人在行情好的时候忍不住多看它两眼，会把一个中性团队的注意力，一点点拉回到方向上。

做市和中性是另一种曲线。
不管市场涨还是跌，它都在走自己的路。赚的时候赚在自己身上，亏的时候亏在自己身上，没有地方可以躲。收益天花板低，单笔利润薄得可怜，要靠执行、基建和日复一日的打磨一点点磨出来。

当然中性也不是无风险。它只是把一个看得见的风险，换成了一堆看不见的风险。方向风险没了，取而代之的是执行、运营和尾部。这也是为什么我们花了那么长时间死磕基建。对做市商来说，基建就是策略本身。

一个团队的精力是有限的。我们想把所有力气，都压在做市和中性上。

但不吃，不代表它没价值。 对一个本来就要做方向、能承受市场波动的团队或资金来说，一个经过实盘验证、回撤可控的 beta 策略，正好是他们缺的那块。东西是好东西，只是放在我们这里，不是最合适的位置。

所以这个策略我们愿意转出去。 如果你正好需要一个方向性的策略，可以私信聊。

不想吃 beta

我们团队的主业是做市和中性策略。

但其实我们手里也有 beta 策略，跑得挺好。曲线漂亮，回撤也在预期里，按收益看，其实很不错的。

最近团队讨论了很久，最后还是决定，不吃这份 beta。

先说清楚 beta 是什么。
beta 是跟着市场赚的钱。

它的收益和市场绑在一起，这对需要方向敞口的人是优点，对我们是负担。它会占用资金和风控额度，会让人在行情好的时候忍不住多看它两眼，会把一个中性团队的注意力，一点点拉回到方向上。

做市和中性是另一种曲线。
不管市场涨还是跌，它都在走自己的路。赚的时候赚在自己身上，亏的时候亏在自己身上，没有地方可以躲。收益天花板低，单笔利润薄得可怜，要靠执行、基建和日复一日的打磨一点点磨出来。

当然中性也不是无风险。它只是把一个看得见的风险，换成了一堆看不见的风险。方向风险没了，取而代之的是执行、运营和尾部。这也是为什么我们花了那么长时间死磕基建。对做市商来说，基建就是策略本身。

一个团队的精力是有限的。我们想把所有力气，都压在做市和中性上。

但不吃，不代表它没价值。 对一个本来就要做方向、能承受市场波动的团队或资金来说，一个经过实盘验证、回撤可控的 beta 策略，正好是他们缺的那块。东西是好东西，只是放在我们这里，不是最合适的位置。

所以这个策略我们愿意转出去。 如果你正好需要一个方向性的策略，可以私信聊。

text:
Agent Evals 最常见的问题都有什么？

@LangChain 团队 @divyasan0 以 Q&A 形式分享了 Agent Evals 实践指南，把常见问题一次性回答了。她给出的可落地工程流程：从真实 trace 起步、小数据集建立基线、失败案例回流迭代、离线/在线分层评估、代码优先于 LLM 裁判、benchmark 用容器化环境验证最终状态。

QA 博客地址：
https://t.co/Uc9QBetiDD

为什么 Agent 难以测试 ？
· 输出不确定性：同一输入，多次运行结果不同；
· 答案非唯一：多个不同回答都可能是正确的，无法做字符串精确匹配；
· 路径自选：Agent 自己决定执行步骤，即使最终答案正确，路径也可能是“错的”（调用了不必要的工具、未经授权就行动）。

起点：从 trace 开始的最小闭环
一条清晰路径值得直接采纳：
读一批真实 trace → 选定一个行为 → 建 10–20 条小数据集 → 跑基线实验 → 之后所有改动都与基线对比。

其中最有价值的工程习惯是失败回流机制：发现一次失败 → 作为新样本加入数据集 → 改进 agent → 重跑全量。这让数据集随系统演化而增长，评估从“一次性验证”变成“持续改进的飞轮”。未上线的团队可以用内部 dogfooding 产生 trace。

离线 vs 在线：两道互补的闸门
· 离线评估（Offline）：发生在发布前、对数据集、用来测新 prompt/模型/工具防回归
· 在线评估（Online）：发生在生产环境、对真实流量 trace、用来持续监控线上质量

两者形成闭环：线上标出的失败，转化为线下的新样本。数据集组织原则也很实用，同一行为、同一组评估器的样本放一起；输入、评估器或目的不同就另建数据集，避免一个大盘子什么都装。

评估器的优先级：代码 > LLM 裁判 > 人工
· 代码评估器：确定性检查（如“价格是否低于预算”），快、便宜、零歧义，能用则必用；
· LLM-as-a-judge：处理代码判不了的主观维度（如“回复是否清晰确认了航班信息”）；
· 人工审核：最贵但最可靠的信号，用于抽样校准前两者；
· Pairwise（成对比较）：让裁判二选一，比绝对打分更稳定。

评估对象的颗粒度也分层：单步 → 最终回复 → 完整对话 → 环境终态（如容器内记录、文件、测试是否通过）。

LLM 裁判能否信任：三条可操作建议
1. 用人工标注对照校准，调整裁判 prompt 直到两者对齐；
2. 问窄问题，“回复是否提到了每一个中转站？”远好于“这是个好回复吗？”；
3. 用二元判定或分类标签，避免 1–10 打分（数值打分的跨 run 一致性很差）。

Eval ≠ Benchmark：一个重要的概念澄清
Benchmark 本质是 “重型离线 eval”，其特殊性在于：
· 任务长链路，涉及数十次工具调用；
· 每个任务自带独立的容器化隔离环境；
· 评分方式是检查运行后的环境状态（订票记录是否存在、代码测试是否通过），而非比对文本。

文中介绍了开源评估 harness Harbor（Terminal-Bench 的底层引擎），每个任务构建一个容器，结果记录到 LangSmith 实验。自建 benchmark 的路径：从 trace 收集任务 → 定义评分规则 → 对分数做 hill climbing（爬山式迭代优化），甚至可以做成 Karpathy 式的自动化研究循环。

线上评估的成本控制
生产流量全量打分不现实，博客给出三层降本：
1. 采样与过滤：只评估有负反馈的 trace；
2. 代码检查优先：几乎零成本；
3. 换更便宜的裁判模型：小模型裁判在 pass/fail 判定上与人类标注一致，总成本 $0.34 vs Claude Sonnet 4.6 的 $28.17（约 1/83）。对二元判定类任务，裁判模型确实不必用旗舰模型。

不必从零自建
生态已提供相当多现成件：针对幻觉、PII 泄露等常见问题的预置 LLM 评估器模板、开源 agentevals 包（针对消息和工具调用）、可从代码仓库和 trace 直接生成可运行评估的 Eval Engineering Skill、从 issue 聚类自动生成数据集和断言的 LangSmith Engine。且整个体系框架无关；支持 OpenAI Agents SDK、Claude Agent SDK，或用 @ traceable 装饰器裸接。

迁移也不必推倒重来：数据集以 CSV/JSONL 导入，pytest/Vitest 集成保留现有测试体系，已有裁判 prompt 直接粘贴复用。

两个进阶难题
多轮对话：每一轮都看似正常、整体却失败的“累积性失败”是单点评估的盲区。解法是给 trace 附上 thread ID 将各轮聚合，再挂载面向整段对话的在线评估器（如“用户是否被迫重复了自己的需求”）；离线侧则把完整对话存为样本，或用 LLM 模拟用户。

超越最终输出：复杂 agent 需要检查轨迹（消息/工具调用序列）与终态（仓库变更、测试结果）。例如编码 agent 跑完后直接在其工作环境里执行该 repo 的测试套件；这正是 Harbor + 容器化沙箱的设计动机。

3. 换更便宜的裁判模型：小模型裁判在 pass/fail 判定上与人类标注一致，总成本 $0.34 vs Claude Sonnet 4.6 的 $28.17（约 1/83）。对二元判定类任务，裁判模型确实不必用旗舰模型。

不必从零自建
生态已提供相当多现成件：针对幻觉、PII 泄露等常见问题的预置 LLM 评估器模板、开源 agentevals 包（针对消息和工具调用）、可从代码仓库和 trace 直接生成可运行评估的 Eval Engineering Skill、从 issue 聚类自动生成数据集和断言的 LangSmith Engine。且整个体系框架无关；支持 OpenAI Agents SDK、Claude Agent SDK，或用 @ traceable 装饰器裸接。

迁移也不必推倒重来：数据集以 CSV/JSONL 导入，pytest/Vitest 集成保留现有测试体系，已有裁判 prompt 直接粘贴复用。

两个进阶难题
多轮对话：每一轮都看似正常、整体却失败的“累积性失败”是单点评估的盲区。解法是给 trace 附上 thread ID 将各轮聚合，再挂载面向整段对话的在线评估器（如“用户是否被迫重复了自己的需求”）；离线侧则把完整对话存为样本，或用 LLM 模拟用户。

超越最终输出：复杂 agent 需要检查轨迹（消息/工具调用序列）与终态（仓库变更、测试结果）。例如编码 agent 跑完后直接在其工作环境里执行该 repo 的测试套件；这正是 Harbor + 容器化沙箱的设计动机。

text:
A lot of people seem confused about what's actually new here, so let me explain.

- ChatGPT can now access information across your open Chrome tabs directly in regular Chat mode, without needing to switch to Work.
- Basically, you can have 10 different tabs open while researching something and ask ChatGPT to cross-reference the information without manually copying and pasting content from each page.
- Previously, the Chrome extension already supported referencing tabs, selecting content, and chatting about webpages through its sidebar. Codex could also interact with Chrome.

What's new today is a more seamless way to bring multiple open tabs into the context of a regular ChatGPT conversation.

Chat is for gathering and understanding information across your tabs. Work goes further, allowing ChatGPT to actually interact with those tabs and complete tasks for you.

quotedTweet.text:
A few big upgrades for Chrome users today! We’re bringing the power of computer use to anyone who uses Chrome.

First up: ChatGPT can now use your tabs in Chrome to make answers more useful and get things done for you. 

If you’re in Chat, it can look across your open tabs and gather info. 

If you’re in Work, ChatGPT can control your Chrome tabs to get things, like sending messages, filling out forms, or downloading files. It can even help you organize and group that pile of tabs you have open.

text:
THIS IS A PURE F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: let Opus 5.5 write the plan as a script, and let a swarm of cheaper agents run it.

Bigger jobs and way fewer Opus tokens, because the script holds the plan and Opus only sees the final answer.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model opus --effort ultracode

here's the split:

→ Opus 5.5 turns your task into a workflow script
→ Haiku 5.5 agents scan every file in parallel
→ Sonnet 5.5 agents patch each fix in its own isolated copy
→ you stop burning Opus context on a hundred agent transcripts

Opus only shows up at three moments:

→ writing the workflow before the run
→ reading the verified results after it
→ signing off before anything ships

Opus plans. Haiku scans. Sonnet ships.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Opus 5.5 runs the main session and writes the workflow
> scan audits every file on Haiku 5.5
> edit patches each fix on Sonnet 5.5 in an isolated copy
> verify cross-checks every finding on Sonnet 5.5
> Opus 5.5 reads only what survived verification
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Opus 5.5 with ultracode on.
2. In every workflow, run read-only scan stages on Haiku 5.5 and edit stages on Sonnet 5.5, each edit in its own isolated copy.
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: every finding gets an independent verifier agent before it's reported, and fix loops stop after two rounds with no progress.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/1MiKDqGANA

save it, it'll come in handy.

text:
Greg Isenberg 在旧金山待了48小时，写了 21 条观察

1、卖数据很赚钱：听到很多数据中介把公司数据卖给实验室、一周赚 200 万美元左右的故事。他分不清这是刚开始还是泡沫，正在研究还剩哪些细分领域。
2、一个灵魂拷问：饭桌上有人问“下个月出新模型，你的公司会变好还是变差”，一半的人答不上来。他认为这是现在评估 AI 创业公司最好的问题。
3、只看收入不看留存：现在大家说的门槛是 12 个月做到 10 亿美元收入（新的独角兽标准），但很少有人谈留存。他预测会出现很多收入很大、留存很差的 AI 公司。
4、很明显我们正在经历计算机的一次重新发明。模型是 CPU，harness 是操作系统，skills 和插件是应用。用这个框架更容易看出哪里还有空白。
5、我们可能离这样一个 agent 只有 12 个月：它看你工作一周，然后不用任何指令就能接手你的活。屏幕录制 + agent 记忆 + 本地模型，这个组合现在就已经能做到了。(可怕）
6、Agent harness 感觉像是新一代的 GPT 套壳，但是好的那种，尤其是垂直领域的。他聊到的最好的团队都把模型当成可替换的零件。比如创始人演示他怎么把不同模型分配给不同任务：一个负责审美和视觉，一个便宜的跑日常杂活，另一个专门处理文本。
7、逆向工程和克隆的事情多到他从没见过。人们在反编译软件，然后用 agent 重建它。有人给他看了一套大概 10 个应用，每个对标的原版都值 50 亿美元以上，全是他开源克隆出来的他和所有人都还在想：当软件变得这么容易复制，到底意味着什么。
8、猜价值会转移到数据上。如果软件可以快速重建，那一家老 SaaS 公司里值得花钱买的，就是里面积累多年的客户数据和工作流。有些 SaaS 公司其实是暗藏的数据公司。
9、感觉相当一部分老软件撑不到 agent 时代，尤其是那些围绕“让人点来点去很多页面”设计的。
10、他聊到的每家公司都想把内部数据汇到一个地方，然后通过 MCP 开放给 agent。然后他们一看数据就发现：一团糟。同一个客户有五个版本，一堆老 Slack 频道，没人能搜到的 PDF。把这些清理干净，感觉是个很大的咨询机会！
11、做积木的公司会赢：很多创始人在做agent用的基础组件，比如 API、数据层和工具。有些公司几乎没有界面，因为主要用户是agent。
12、实验室不缺训练数据，但很难拿到 agent 在企业内部出错的真实案例。谁手里有这些日志，谁就有值钱的东西。
13、一个做大型消费产品的人说，下一场仗是记忆。记住你最多的那个模型会赢，最聪明的模型没有大家想的那么重要。
14、Astra 是第一个让人相信 AI 能做 CAD 的模型，大家开始想“vibe 制造”是什么样子。一位机器人创始人说：现在 AI 最难的问题是部署问题，不是研究问题。他们的机器人自己干活，卡住了就呼叫人类，而每一次呼叫都变成训练数据。
15、网络安全公司正在迎来高光时刻，现在做这个真的很酷，尤其是那些做事后清理的。每一个能访问你系统的 agent 都是你公司的一扇新门，而且很多门就那么敞着。
16、死了比活着值钱：倒闭公司 5 年的 Slack、邮件和代码可以拿去授权收钱。他不意外创始人会把这一点算进关停时机。
17、人们开始聊“agent 互联网”怎么变现。感觉还非常早，但当互联网最活跃的用户变成 agent，你应该做什么样的创业公司？
18、agent 保险要来了。一旦智能体犯了昂贵的错，保险公司会要求先审计再承保。
19、好几个人说他们最想招的人，是有品味又会写 evals 的人。模型越来越会出点子了，难的是判断哪些点子是好的。
20、新的创业轨迹：拿 VC 的钱 → 用投资人的钱把自己做成网红 → 公司失败 → 创始人转成全职网红，再用自有资金孵化别的产品。
21、流量极难拿：创始人们在赞助公交车、疯狂买广告牌、请知名 DJ 办派对，就为了被看见。有点互联网泡沫时代那味儿了。真正稀缺的是注意力！那个靠分享 Wispr Flow 的 UGC 策略走红的增长负责人就是个好例子。这就是所有人都想要的秘方，全世界大概只有 50 个人知道怎么在这个时代高效地把这类生意做大。

每次去旧金山，回来总能受到不少刺激。能在这样一个创业的黄金时刻，经历这么精彩的一趟旅程，他觉得自己太幸运了。很多时候，甚至有种不真实的感觉。
写的真好！分享给大家！
（他说是跟一群亿万富翁、数据实验室的人、AI 创始人和高管的交流）

quotedTweet.text:
I spent 48 hours in SF hanging out with billionaires, data labs and AI founders and execs running $1B to $100B companies.

My observations:

1. Sooo MANY stories of data brokers making like $2M a WEEK selling company data to labs. I can't tell if it's the beginning or a bubble, and I kept wondering which niches are left. Digging into it actively.

2. At dinner, someone asked the table, "If a new model drops next month, does your company get better or worse?" HALF the table went quiet! I think that's the best question to ask about any AI startup right now.

3. The bar people talk about now is hitting $1B in revenue in 12 months (I guess that's the new unicorn?). What I didn't hear much about is retention. AI revenue can come in fast and leave fast, and I think we're going to see a lot of stories of AI companies with huge revenue and terrible retention.

4. It's pretty clear we're living through the reinvention of the computer. The model is the CPU, the harness is the operating system, and skills and plugins are the apps. Thinking about it that way makes it easier to see where the whitespace is.

5. We're maybe 12 months from an agent that can watch you work for a week and then do your job without any instructions. The screen recording plus agent memory plus local model combination makes this possible right now.

6. Agent harnesses feel like the new GPT wrappers, in a good way, especially vertical ones. The best teams I talked to treat the model as swappable. One founder walked me through routing different models to different jobs: one for taste and visuals, a cheaper one for the everyday stuff, another for text. 

They use prompts they can move across models over fine-tuning, and A/B test the output on what users actually do with it: do they edit it, export it, share it? A vertical harness is basically four things: the connectors for that industry's data, evals written by people who know the work, rules for what the agent can and can't touch, and a clean screen for a human to review. The model is maybe 20% of it.

7. There's a lot of reverse engineering going on/cloning going on more than I've ever seen. People are decompiling software and rebuilding it with agents, and someone showed a suite of like 10 apps that are worth $5B+ each all that he cloned open source. Me and everyone are still thinking through what it means when software gets this easy to copy.

8. My guess is the value moves to data. If the software can be rebuilt quickly, what's worth paying for in a legacy SaaS company is the years of customer data and workflows inside it. Some SaaS companies are secretly data companies. 

Gets me thinking about how do you truly value data for this saas companies? Like if we were buying these dying saas companies at 2x ARR before (as example), maybe there is a better metric. Idk, just thinking out loud here.

9. It feels like a good chunk of legacy software won't make it to the agentic era, especially anything built around people clicking through a lot of screens.

10. Every company I talked to wants to pipe its internal data into one place and expose it to agents through MCP. Then they look at the data and realize it's a mess: five versions of the same customer, old Slack channels, PDFs nobody can search. Cleaning that up feels like a big consulting opportunity!

11. A lot of founders are building the basic building blocks for agents: APIs, data layers and tools. Some of the companies I saw barely have a UI because the main user is an agent. I really believe the startups that build primitives to this agentic era will do extremely well. Building blocks is the best way to think about it.

12. Labs can get plenty of training data, but it's harder to get real examples of agents failing inside companies. Whoever has those logs has something valuable.

13. Someone running a big consumer company told me the next fight is over memory. The model that remembers the most about you wins, and the smartest model matters less than people think.

14. Physical AI came up a lot. Astra I think was the first model that got people into AI can actually do CAD, and I think a lot of people are thinking what does vibe manufacturing really look like. The line I keep thinking about came from a robotics founder: the hardest problems in AI are deployment problems now, not research problems. Their robots work on their own, call a human when they get stuck, and every one of those calls becomes training data.

15. Cybersecurity companies are having a moment and are actually cool companies to build now, especially the ones that clean up after a breach. Every agent with access to your systems is a new door into your company, and a lot of those doors were left open. 

16. Some startups are worth more dead than alive now. A shutdown company with 5 years of Slack, email and code can get paid for licensing all of it. I wouldn't be surprised if founders start factoring that into when they shut down.

17. People are starting to talk about monetizing the agent web. It feels really early, but when the most popular user of the internet is an agent, what startups should you be building?

18. I think agent insurance is coming. Once an agent makes an expensive mistake, insurers will want audits before they cover anyone.

19. Several people said the hire they want most is someone with taste who can write evals. The models are getting good at generating ideas, so the hard part is judging which ones are good.

20. New trend I observed: startup raises VC, uses venture dollars to become a creator, startup fails, founder falls back on being a full-time creator and incubates other products bootstrapped.

21. Getting SIGNIFICANT distribution is HARD right now. Founders are sponsoring buses, buying billboards like crazy and throwing parties with famous DJs to get noticed. Kinda feels dotcom era in that sense. 

Attention is what's scarce! The growth guy going viral sharing his UGC strategy from Wispr Flow is a good example. It's the sauce everyone wants, and I truly believe there are probably only 50 people on the planet who know how to scale these types of businesses efficiently in this era.

Always good to get that dose of SF. I felt sooo lucky to have such an incredible trip during such an incredible time in building businesses. Surreal in so many ways. 

Happy to be home and locked in.

Until next time!

7、逆向工程和克隆的事情多到他从没见过。人们在反编译软件，然后用 agent 重建它。有人给他看了一套大概 10 个应用，每个对标的原版都值 50 亿美元以上，全是他开源克隆出来的他和所有人都还在想：当软件变得这么容易复制，到底意味着什么。
8、猜价值会转移到数据上。如果软件可以快速重建，那一家老 SaaS 公司里值得花钱买的，就是里面积累多年的客户数据和工作流。有些 SaaS 公司其实是暗藏的数据公司。
9、感觉相当一部分老软件撑不到 agent 时代，尤其是那些围绕“让人点来点去很多页面”设计的。
10、他聊到的每家公司都想把内部数据汇到一个地方，然后通过 MCP 开放给 agent。然后他们一看数据就发现：一团糟。同一个客户有五个版本，一堆老 Slack 频道，没人能搜到的 PDF。把这些清理干净，感觉是个很大的咨询机会！
11、做积木的公司会赢：很多创始人在做agent用的基础组件，比如 API、数据层和工具。有些公司几乎没有界面，因为主要用户是agent。
12、实验室不缺训练数据，但很难拿到 agent 在企业内部出错的真实案例。谁手里有这些日志，谁就有值钱的东西。
13、一个做大型消费产品的人说，下一场仗是记忆。记住你最多的那个模型会赢，最聪明的模型没有大家想的那么重要。
14、Astra 是第一个让人相信 AI 能做 CAD 的模型，大家开始想“vibe 制造”是什么样子。一位机器人创始人说：现在 AI 最难的问题是部署问题，不是研究问题。他们的机器人自己干活，卡住了就呼叫人类，而每一次呼叫都变成训练数据。
15、网络安全公司正在迎来高光时刻，现在做这个真的很酷，尤其是那些做事后清理的。每一个能访问你系统的 agent 都是你公司的一扇新门，而且很多门就那么敞着。
16、死了比活着值钱：倒闭公司 5 年的 Slack、邮件和代码可以拿去授权收钱。他不意外创始人会把这一点算进关停时机。
17、人们开始聊“agent 互联网”怎么变现。感觉还非常早，但当互联网最活跃的用户变成 agent，你应该做什么样的创业公司？
18、agent 保险要来了。一旦智能体犯了昂贵的错，保险公司会要求先审计再承保。
19、好几个人说他们最想招的人，是有品味又会写 evals 的人。模型越来越会出点子了，难的是判断哪些点子是好的。
20、新的创业轨迹：拿 VC 的钱 → 用投资人的钱把自己做成网红 → 公司失败 → 创始人转成全职网红，再用自有资金孵化别的产品。
21、流量极难拿：创始人们在赞助公交车、疯狂买广告牌、请知名 DJ 办派对，就为了被看见。有点互联网泡沫时代那味儿了。真正稀缺的是注意力！那个靠分享 Wispr Flow 的 UGC 策略走红的增长负责人就是个好例子。这就是所有人都想要的秘方，全世界大概只有 50 个人知道怎么在这个时代高效地把这类生意做大。

每次去旧金山，回来总能受到不少刺激。能在这样一个创业的黄金时刻，经历这么精彩的一趟旅程，他觉得自己太幸运了。很多时候，甚至有种不真实的感觉。
写的真好！分享给大家！
（他说是跟一群亿万富翁、数据实验室的人、AI 创始人和高管的交流）

result.text:
I spent 48 hours in SF hanging out with billionaires, data labs and AI founders and execs running $1B to $100B companies.

My observations:

1. Sooo MANY stories of data brokers making like $2M a WEEK selling company data to labs. I can't tell if it's the beginning or a bubble, and I kept wondering which niches are left. Digging into it actively.

2. At dinner, someone asked the table, "If a new model drops next month, does your company get better or worse?" HALF the table went quiet! I think that's the best question to ask about any AI startup right now.

3. The bar people talk about now is hitting $1B in revenue in 12 months (I guess that's the new unicorn?). What I didn't hear much about is retention. AI revenue can come in fast and leave fast, and I think we're going to see a lot of stories of AI companies with huge revenue and terrible retention.

4. It's pretty clear we're living through the reinvention of the computer. The model is the CPU, the harness is the operating system, and skills and plugins are the apps. Thinking about it that way makes it easier to see where the whitespace is.

5. We're maybe 12 months from an agent that can watch you work for a week and then do your job without any instructions. The screen recording plus agent memory plus local model combination makes this possible right now.

6. Agent harnesses feel like the new GPT wrappers, in a good way, especially vertical ones. The best teams I talked to treat the model as swappable. One founder walked me through routing different models to different jobs: one for taste and visuals, a cheaper one for the everyday stuff, another for text. 

They use prompts they can move across models over fine-tuning, and A/B test the output on what users actually do with it: do they edit it, export it, share it? A vertical harness is basically four things: the connectors for that industry's data, evals written by people who know the work, rules for what the agent can and can't touch, and a clean screen for a human to review. The model is maybe 20% of it.

7. There's a lot of reverse engineering going on/cloning going on more than I've ever seen. People are decompiling software and rebuilding it with agents, and someone showed a suite of like 10 apps that are worth $5B+ each all that he cloned open source. Me and everyone are still thinking through what it means when software gets this easy to copy.

8. My guess is the value moves to data. If the software can be rebuilt quickly, what's worth paying for in a legacy SaaS company is the years of customer data and workflows inside it. Some SaaS companies are secretly data companies. 

Gets me thinking about how do you truly value data for this saas companies? Like if we were buying these dying saas companies at 2x ARR before (as example), maybe there is a better metric. Idk, just thinking out loud here.

9. It feels like a good chunk of legacy software won't make it to the agentic era, especially anything built around people clicking through a lot of screens.

10. Every company I talked to wants to pipe its internal data into one place and expose it to agents through MCP. Then they look at the data and realize it's a mess: five versions of the same customer, old Slack channels, PDFs nobody can search. Cleaning that up feels like a big consulting opportunity!

11. A lot of founders are building the basic building blocks for agents: APIs, data layers and tools. Some of the companies I saw barely have a UI because the main user is an agent. I really believe the startups that build primitives to this agentic era will do extremely well. Building blocks is the best way to think about it.

12. Labs can get plenty of training data, but it's harder to get real examples of agents failing inside companies. Whoever has those logs has something valuable.

13. Someone running a big consumer company told me the next fight is over memory. The model that remembers the most about you wins, and the smartest model matters less than people think.

14. Physical AI came up a lot. Astra I think was the first model that got people into AI can actually do CAD, and I think a lot of people are thinking what does vibe manufacturing really look like. The line I keep thinking about came from a robotics founder: the hardest problems in AI are deployment problems now, not research problems. Their robots work on their own, call a human when they get stuck, and every one of those calls becomes training data.

15. Cybersecurity companies are having a moment and are actually cool companies to build now, especially the ones that clean up after a breach. Every agent with access to your systems is a new door into your company, and a lot of those doors were left open. 

16. Some startups are worth more dead than alive now. A shutdown company with 5 years of Slack, email and code can get paid for licensing all of it. I wouldn't be surprised if founders start factoring that into when they shut down.

17. People are starting to talk about monetizing the agent web. It feels really early, but when the most popular user of the internet is an agent, what startups should you be building?

18. I think agent insurance is coming. Once an agent makes an expensive mistake, insurers will want audits before they cover anyone.

19. Several people said the hire they want most is someone with taste who can write evals. The models are getting good at generating ideas, so the hard part is judging which ones are good.

20. New trend I observed: startup raises VC, uses venture dollars to become a creator, startup fails, founder falls back on being a full-time creator and incubates other products bootstrapped.

21. Getting SIGNIFICANT distribution is HARD right now. Founders are sponsoring buses, buying billboards like crazy and throwing parties with famous DJs to get noticed. Kinda feels dotcom era in that sense. 

Attention is what's scarce! The growth guy going viral sharing his UGC strategy from Wispr Flow is a good example. It's the sauce everyone wants, and I truly believe there are probably only 50 people on the planet who know how to scale these types of businesses efficiently in this era.

Always good to get that dose of SF. I felt sooo lucky to have such an incredible trip during such an incredible time in building businesses. Surreal in so many ways. 

Happy to be home and locked in.

Until next time!

我调研了一圈方案
纯 ACP 要实现的东西太多、Raft 团队的 oar 好一些，暴露面不够
t3code（https://t.co/fuHWAbZDlt）是综合看下来最好的，本身就是多 Harness 的 ADE，同时本身就是 server-client 分离，可以根据自己的需求复用API，也可以直接拿 t3code client 当看板（有移动端）
更惊喜的是，这个 ADE 本身的所有面向人的交互都被保证成了 MCP 可以给 bot 无缝接入

另外这个项目的维护方式非常激进，迭代速度极快（质量很好），值得学习

text:
旧金山现在最反乌托邦的画面，可能是一个老板打开 Slack，看着一群 AI Agent 互相汇报工作，整个频道里只有他一个活人。

Greg Isenberg 刚从旧金山回来，写了 20 条观察。我看完觉得挺有意思，有些变化已经远远超出了 AI 产品本身。

比如，现在旧金山的广告牌上已经开始出现 inference 这种技术术语，而美国绝大多数普通人可能连 Agent 是什么都不知道。创业者以前喜欢炫耀自己招了多少人，现在开始炫耀人均营收。22 岁以下的年轻人正在赚到令人难以置信的钱，小团队带着一群 Agent 就能运转一家公司的场景也越来越常见。

其中我最感兴趣的是他提到的一句话，现在一个产品需要完成两次销售，第一次是让 Agent 选择你，第二次是让人类相信 Agent 的选择。

我觉得这件事可能会彻底改变软件行业的商业逻辑。过去的产品围绕人类用户设计获客、营销、定价和支付流程。等到 Agent 开始替人搜索、比较、采购甚至付款，软件公司的第一个客户很可能就变成了另一个软件。

他还特意给 Manus 点了个赞。2025 年 3 月，Manus 就已经做出了今天大量 Agent 产品都在使用的交互范式，给每个任务分配一台云端电脑，展示执行过程，列出任务清单并逐项完成，人类可以离开电脑等结果。我觉得这个评价挺高的，尤其是来自一个长期观察硅谷创业生态的人。

还有几个观察值得放在一起看。

AI 让自由职业者和代理机构的工作效率提高了数倍，但很多人依然按小时收费。客户迟早会发现，同样的工作现在只需要原来五分之一的时间，那你到底应该收多少钱？

员工开始自己用 AI 写各种小工具，公司 IT 部门甚至不知道内部到底运行着多少软件。过去企业花钱买标准化 SaaS，现在每个人都在给自己开发软件。

更有意思的是，Greg 还遇到一个人，认真跟他说应该把所有数据中心都毁掉。

旧金山的创业者已经在讨论 2027 年 Agent 能不能主动发现航班延误、自动完成改签，外面却有人恨不得直接把数据中心拆了。AI 公司越来越喜欢宣传治愈癌症、让人类拥有更多自由时间，某种程度上也说明它们开始意识到，社会对 AI 的情绪正在分化。

我觉得 Greg 这 20 条观察里真正值得关注的，是 AI 已经开始重新定义一家公司的组织方式、定价方式和竞争方式。

不过旧金山可能也正在形成一个巨大的认知泡沫。他提到，全美只有大约 2% 的人在为 AI 产品付费，旧金山却给人一种 110% 的人都在付费的错觉。

一座城市已经开始讨论 Agent 之间怎么做生意，更多人还没搞明白 AI 到底能给自己的生活带来什么。

这中间的距离，可能才是未来几年 AI 行业真正需要跨越的东西。

quotedTweet.text:
More SF observations:

1. Seeing the word "inference" on billboards in SF still blows my mind. 99.9% of america has no idea what inference is and I wonder how many know what an agent is. Will Muse, Instinct, Dots etc will change that over the next 12 months?

2. You know who doesn't get enough credit? Manus. In March 2025 they shipped the blueprint for AI agents: every task gets its own computer in the cloud, you can watch it work, it writes a todo list and checks it off, and you walk away while it finishes. So much of what we use today runs on those ideas!

3. Your product now has to sell itself twice. First the agent has to pick it, then the human has to trust that pick enough to say yes.

4. I was talking to a guy who told me we should just destroy all the data centers. I think that sentiment is more common than people in SF realize. You can already see some of the big AI companies adjusting positioning their AI as something that helps people and gives them more time/cures for cancers etc.

5. AI is making people work 5x faster (at least), so for freelancers/agencies that charge per hour you're earning 5x less per unit of work. But your rate is the same? I think a lot of freelancers and agencies are about to have to rethink how they price.

6. Running a company now feels kinda dystopian sometimes, especially with a small team of a few humans and a lot of agents. Some days the Slack channel is mostly bots reporting to each other, and you're the only one in the room with a pulse.

7. Every product company is turning into a product studio. I see it firsthand as a co-founder of @meetLCA , which is basically a Labs as a Service company incubating new products for companies. (DM me if you want to work together in 2027).

8. Personal software is exploding. People at every company are building their own little tools for their own jobs. It's amazing for productivity and a nightmare for IT, because nobody knows what's running or who owns it.

9. Revenue per human is the new flex. Founders used to brag about headcount. Now they brag about how much they're doing with how few people.

11. More founders are using agents for customer research. Agents run the interviews, read every support ticket and summarize what people are begging for. Synthetic market research is the new thing.

12. Shipping technology that actually takes 3-6 months with unique partnerships that are hard to replicate. So, partnerships are sooo back!

13. Insane amount of young people (22 or younger) making absurds amounts of money. At least it feels that way.  Never seen anything like that, even during mobile era.

14. Only 2% of the US is paying for AI products, but it feels like 110% SF is.

15. Advice for college grads used to be “follow your passion” and now it’s follow careers that are not  document- driven, rules-bound and verifiable

16. Seeing the word inference on billboards in SF still blows my mind.

17. Agents paying for things feels futuristic. I think its coming, only a matter of time, but  I’m wondering when it becomes mainstream. 2027?

18. Lots of talk about proactive agents being the next phase of personal agents. Right now you ask your agent to do something. In 2027, it’s all going to be about noticing things (context/memory) and acting first. "Your flight got delayed, I already rebooked you."

19. The quote "what the smartest people do on the weekend is what everyone else will do during the week in 10 years." by Chris Dixon. It feels like that length of time isnt 10 years anymore, its 12 months.

20. This is the most asymmetric window I've ever seen in business.

My DMs are open. Respond to the most interesting ones.

Loved my trip to SF. Until next time. Maybe NYC next?

Thank you for everything.

I'm rooting for you.

20. This is the most asymmetric window I've ever seen in business.

result.text:
旧金山现在最反乌托邦的画面，可能是一个老板打开 Slack，看着一群 AI Agent 互相汇报工作，整个频道里只有他一个活人。

Greg Isenberg 刚从旧金山回来，写了 20 条观察。我看完觉得挺有意思，有些变化已经远远超出了 AI 产品本身。

比如，现在旧金山的广告牌上已经开始出现 inference 这种技术术语，而美国绝大多数普通人可能连 Agent 是什么都不知道。创业者以前喜欢炫耀自己招了多少人，现在开始炫耀人均营收。22 岁以下的年轻人正在赚到令人难以置信的钱，小团队带着一群 Agent 就能运转一家公司的场景也越来越常见。

其中我最感兴趣的是他提到的一句话，现在一个产品需要完成两次销售，第一次是让 Agent 选择你，第二次是让人类相信 Agent 的选择。

我觉得这件事可能会彻底改变软件行业的商业逻辑。过去的产品围绕人类用户设计获客、营销、定价和支付流程。等到 Agent 开始替人搜索、比较、采购甚至付款，软件公司的第一个客户很可能就变成了另一个软件。

他还特意给 Manus 点了个赞。2025 年 3 月，Manus 就已经做出了今天大量 Agent 产品都在使用的交互范式，给每个任务分配一台云端电脑，展示执行过程，列出任务清单并逐项完成，人类可以离开电脑等结果。我觉得这个评价挺高的，尤其是来自一个长期观察硅谷创业生态的人。

还有几个观察值得放在一起看。

AI 让自由职业者和代理机构的工作效率提高了数倍，但很多人依然按小时收费。客户迟早会发现，同样的工作现在只需要原来五分之一的时间，那你到底应该收多少钱？

员工开始自己用 AI 写各种小工具，公司 IT 部门甚至不知道内部到底运行着多少软件。过去企业花钱买标准化 SaaS，现在每个人都在给自己开发软件。

更有意思的是，Greg 还遇到一个人，认真跟他说应该把所有数据中心都毁掉。

旧金山的创业者已经在讨论 2027 年 Agent 能不能主动发现航班延误、自动完成改签，外面却有人恨不得直接把数据中心拆了。AI 公司越来越喜欢宣传治愈癌症、让人类拥有更多自由时间，某种程度上也说明它们开始意识到，社会对 AI 的情绪正在分化。

我觉得 Greg 这 20 条观察里真正值得关注的，是 AI 已经开始重新定义一家公司的组织方式、定价方式和竞争方式。

不过旧金山可能也正在形成一个巨大的认知泡沫。他提到，全美只有大约 2% 的人在为 AI 产品付费，旧金山却给人一种 110% 的人都在付费的错觉。

一座城市已经开始讨论 Agent 之间怎么做生意，更多人还没搞明白 AI 到底能给自己的生活带来什么。

这中间的距离，可能才是未来几年 AI 行业真正需要跨越的东西。

More SF observations:

1. Seeing the word "inference" on billboards in SF still blows my mind. 99.9% of america has no idea what inference is and I wonder how many know what an agent is. Will Muse, Instinct, Dots etc will change that over the next 12 months?

2. You know who doesn't get enough credit? Manus. In March 2025 they shipped the blueprint for AI agents: every task gets its own computer in the cloud, you can watch it work, it writes a todo list and checks it off, and you walk away while it finishes. So much of what we use today runs on those ideas!

3. Your product now has to sell itself twice. First the agent has to pick it, then the human has to trust that pick enough to say yes.

4. I was talking to a guy who told me we should just destroy all the data centers. I think that sentiment is more common than people in SF realize. You can already see some of the big AI companies adjusting positioning their AI as something that helps people and gives them more time/cures for cancers etc.

5. AI is making people work 5x faster (at least), so for freelancers/agencies that charge per hour you're earning 5x less per unit of work. But your rate is the same? I think a lot of freelancers and agencies are about to have to rethink how they price.

6. Running a company now feels kinda dystopian sometimes, especially with a small team of a few humans and a lot of agents. Some days the Slack channel is mostly bots reporting to each other, and you're the only one in the room with a pulse.

7. Every product company is turning into a product studio. I see it firsthand as a co-founder of @meetLCA , which is basically a Labs as a Service company incubating new products for companies. (DM me if you want to work together in 2027).

8. Personal software is exploding. People at every company are building their own little tools for their own jobs. It's amazing for productivity and a nightmare for IT, because nobody knows what's running or who owns it.

9. Revenue per human is the new flex. Founders used to brag about headcount. Now they brag about how much they're doing with how few people.

11. More founders are using agents for customer research. Agents run the interviews, read every support ticket and summarize what people are begging for. Synthetic market research is the new thing.

12. Shipping technology that actually takes 3-6 months with unique partnerships that are hard to replicate. So, partnerships are sooo back!

13. Insane amount of young people (22 or younger) making absurds amounts of money. At least it feels that way.  Never seen anything like that, even during mobile era.

14. Only 2% of the US is paying for AI products, but it feels like 110% SF is.

15. Advice for college grads used to be “follow your passion” and now it’s follow careers that are not  document- driven, rules-bound and verifiable

16. Seeing the word inference on billboards in SF still blows my mind.

17. Agents paying for things feels futuristic. I think its coming, only a matter of time, but  I’m wondering when it becomes mainstream. 2027?

18. Lots of talk about proactive agents being the next phase of personal agents. Right now you ask your agent to do something. In 2027, it’s all going to be about noticing things (context/memory) and acting first. "Your flight got delayed, I already rebooked you."

19. The quote "what the smartest people do on the weekend is what everyone else will do during the week in 10 years." by Chris Dixon. It feels like that length of time isnt 10 years anymore, its 12 months.

20. This is the most asymmetric window I've ever seen in business.

My DMs are open. Respond to the most interesting ones.

Loved my trip to SF. Until next time. Maybe NYC next?

I'm rooting for you.

text:
马斯克原本挺想跟比尔·盖茨交朋友的，结果2022年见了一面，两人就彻底闹翻了。  

盖茨想拉马斯克一起做慈善，马斯克觉得大部分慈善都是狗屁，还质问他：“你是不是还拿着5亿美元的特斯拉空头？”

随后，马斯克又在推特上发了荤段子，配着一张盖茨挺着大肚子的照片🤣

其实一直以来，在马斯克心里，盖茨一直和自己是同一类人，都是靠技术白手起家的硬核工程师。
所以2022年3月，盖茨说想来聊聊慈善和气候，马斯克很爽快地答应了，还带他参观了特斯拉的得州工厂。  

可刚走进工厂，两人就杠上了。 
盖茨直接说，电池永远带不动大卡车，太阳能也成不了解决气候问题的主力，还拿出数据，觉得在这方面自己显然比马斯克懂得多。 
聊到火星，盖茨更是觉得马斯克的想法有点疯狂。  

两个人都习惯了自己是屋子里最聪明的那个，也都受不了别人犯蠢，这一聊，谁也说服不了谁。  

到了慈善上，分歧就更大了。 
马斯克觉得大部分慈善都是“狗屁”，每捐1美元，真正起作用的只有20美分，还不如把钱投进特斯拉，让更多人开上电动车，对气候的帮助大得多。 

盖茨却拿出五个项目，每个1亿美元，想说服他。  

而真正让马斯克过不去的，是盖茨做空了特斯拉。 
盖茨押特斯拉股价会跌，到奥斯汀的时候已经亏了15亿美元，他也为此道了歉。 
可在马斯克看来，一边说自己关心气候，一边做空在这方面贡献最大的公司，这就是虚伪。 

4月，盖茨把亲手写好的慈善方案发了过来。 马斯克一个字没提慈善，只问了一句：“你是不是还拿着5亿美元的特斯拉空头？” 

盖茨承认还没平仓，想把话题拉回慈善合作上，马斯克直接回绝：“对不起！你持有大量特斯拉空头，我没法认真对待你在气候上的慈善。”  

骂完还不解气，他又发了那张大肚子照片🤣  

后来再说起盖茨，马斯克还是一肚子火，说他在这件事上就是个疯子，说白了就是个浑蛋。 
可说完，他又叹了口气：“我确实是想跟他交朋友来着。”

result.text:
马斯克原本挺想跟比尔·盖茨交朋友的，结果2022年见了一面，两人就彻底闹翻了。  

盖茨想拉马斯克一起做慈善，马斯克觉得大部分慈善都是狗屁，还质问他：“你是不是还拿着5亿美元的特斯拉空头？”

随后，马斯克又在推特上发了荤段子，配着一张盖茨挺着大肚子的照片🤣

其实一直以来，在马斯克心里，盖茨一直和自己是同一类人，都是靠技术白手起家的硬核工程师。
所以2022年3月，盖茨说想来聊聊慈善和气候，马斯克很爽快地答应了，还带他参观了特斯拉的得州工厂。  

可刚走进工厂，两人就杠上了。 
盖茨直接说，电池永远带不动大卡车，太阳能也成不了解决气候问题的主力，还拿出数据，觉得在这方面自己显然比马斯克懂得多。 
聊到火星，盖茨更是觉得马斯克的想法有点疯狂。  

两个人都习惯了自己是屋子里最聪明的那个，也都受不了别人犯蠢，这一聊，谁也说服不了谁。  

到了慈善上，分歧就更大了。 
马斯克觉得大部分慈善都是“狗屁”，每捐1美元，真正起作用的只有20美分，还不如把钱投进特斯拉，让更多人开上电动车，对气候的帮助大得多。 

盖茨却拿出五个项目，每个1亿美元，想说服他。  

而真正让马斯克过不去的，是盖茨做空了特斯拉。 
盖茨押特斯拉股价会跌，到奥斯汀的时候已经亏了15亿美元，他也为此道了歉。 
可在马斯克看来，一边说自己关心气候，一边做空在这方面贡献最大的公司，这就是虚伪。 

4月，盖茨把亲手写好的慈善方案发了过来。 马斯克一个字没提慈善，只问了一句：“你是不是还拿着5亿美元的特斯拉空头？” 

盖茨承认还没平仓，想把话题拉回慈善合作上，马斯克直接回绝：“对不起！你持有大量特斯拉空头，我没法认真对待你在气候上的慈善。”  

骂完还不解气，他又发了那张大肚子照片🤣  

后来再说起盖茨，马斯克还是一肚子火，说他在这件事上就是个疯子，说白了就是个浑蛋。 
可说完，他又叹了口气：“我确实是想跟他交朋友来着。”

text:
An overview of how we think about context graphs at @harvey. 

Context graphs are a promising direction for improving agent quality and efficiency. We ran a series of experiments on Legal Agent Bench to evaluate how structured context improves online agent performance.

For each LAB task we evaluated, an agent first reviews each document in its client matter and builds a graph of relevant entities and their relationships – e.g. parties, dates, draft vs. executed status, which versions belong to the same contract.

To evaluate the impact of the graph, we compared the performance of an agent with and without the context graph, using LAB’s standard grading setup. Overall, the agent with the context graph improved rubric pass rate by up to 30% while reducing task cost by up to ~50%.

In some cases the graph led to massive improvements. For example, in one firm-knowledge task, the agent was asked to find the firm’s most recent secured financing and retrieve the executed credit and security agreements as precedents for a new facility.

An agent working from raw files attempted to search through several files sequentially, and looked at many different matters, but ultimately selected the wrong precedent (0% of rubric criteria). With the context graph, the same agent found the relevant matter and its executed agreements immediately (75% of rubric criteria).

We’ll have more to share soon on how we’re building this into Harvey, along with more experiments like this one!

text:
Cheng Lou 开源 Handwired：手写权重，把程序逻辑变成不用训练的神经网络

Midjourney 工程师、前 React 核心团队成员 Cheng Lou 开源了一个自称“玩具项目”的 Handwired：把程序里的 if-else 和循环改写成神经网络的权重。权重是手写的，不用训练，输出和对应的 JavaScript 程序完全一致，在浏览器里就能跑。

原理一行代码就能讲清。比如 result = a > 4 ? 10 : 12，在 a 是整数时可以改写成：

above4 = relu(a - 4) - relu(a - 5)
result = above4 × 10 + (1 - above4) × 12

relu 就是 Math.max(0, x)，神经网络里最常见的激活函数。a 大于 4 时 above4 正好是 1，否则是 0。两个分支都算出来，再用它挑一个。神经网络本质上就是一堆乘法、加法加上 relu，所以程序里的判断和分支，都能收进一个大矩阵乘法里。

也许你会好奇，神经网络的输出不是带概率、不精确吗？

Cheng Lou 的回答是：训练出来的才这样，按程序逻辑手写的权重，同样的输入永远得到同样的输出。

他放了三个 demo。

第一个是 Mini OS，一个有三个窗口和程序坞的小桌面，拖动、缩放、层叠、滚动、文字输入、动画都有。打开浏览器开发者工具看，页面就是普通的网页元素，没有大模型，也没有扩散模型。驱动它的是一个 130 层、9909 个权重的“神经网络”，训练次数为零，在浏览器里用 CPU 实时计算。

第二个是实时搜索 10 万份 JSON 文档，每敲一个键重搜一遍。正则匹配、JSON 解析、高亮全是这种手写网络，再转成 WebGPU 代码放到显卡上并行跑。项目文档里的实测（Apple M5 Max + Chrome）：每次搜索 11 到 15 毫秒；浏览器自带的正则引擎一般 8 到 28 毫秒，遇到容易回溯的写法要 2 秒多。文档写明两者谁快说不准，所以页面把两个时间都列出来。浏览器不支持 WebGPU 时会退回 CPU，搜一遍要 13 秒。

第三个是会“学习”的相册。整个程序可微分，也就是能用训练神经网络的反向传播来调参数。你在左边画几个矩形当草图，右边的照片布局由一个小网络算出，它的 244 个参数随着你拖动实时训练。损失函数里加了一项对齐惩罚，照片会自己往一条线上靠，没有任何代码专门去对齐它们。参数很少，训练全在 JavaScript 里跑。

Cheng Lou 还设想，把一段 Handwired 程序接到 nanoGPT（Andrej Karpathy 的一个小型 GPT 训练项目）这样的模型上一起训练，模型既能写莎士比亚，又能精确执行那段程序。这个目前只是 README 里的设想，仓库里没有现成实现。

代码以 MIT 许可开源，demo 直接在网页上打开就能玩。想自己写，需要装 Bun，克隆仓库后从 template 目录的开关按钮示例开始，文档里有完整教程。

推文说“把普通 JS 代码变成神经网络”，容易让人以为能把现成代码丢进去自动转换。项目文档写的是：没有工具能把已有的 JavaScript 源码转成网络。你要用它提供的构建函数，把逻辑一句句写成比较、选择、加权求和这类操作。网络每次都要把所有操作跑一遍，不能提前退出，也不能跑运行时才知道次数的循环，所以常见的循环得改写成计数、树形合并之类的结构，文档专门用一章讲怎么改。所有数都是 32 位浮点数，每个值的取值范围要事先声明。

项目主页：https://t.co/ywg9dzrFbM
GitHub：https://t.co/fg1sj0trv4
原推文：https://t.co/QW2cMnSiWE

burnout 不是系统坏了，是它在喊停。

Lauren 离开 React 核心团队后休息一个月，随手写的 side project，后来成了 pstack。她当时觉得那些 skill 没用了——进 Cursor 做 Grok Bot，才发现 verification 那套教训一直在。

很多人把休息当浪费。真正拉开差距的，往往是停下来时写下的判断标准：agent 不能只「看起来对」，要自己跑通、自己验。

你也一样：累的时候别急着硬扛，先把「怎样算做完」写清楚。那几行字，比再多敲一小时更值钱。

text:
网上夸他的太多了，说说不一样的视角 —— 陈光宇待了1年后从Kimi离职，这位17岁离开 Kimi 的天才少年，1年离职也比较正常。

首先人家肯定厉害。16岁被 Kimi 招进去，论文并列一作，人家的很多成绩，我们很多普通人都做不到。观点的角度，不涉及任何贬低的意思。

人家才17岁，非常聪明，父母认知肯定也是顶级。在17岁基本走了一遍研究生、甚至博士要做的事情，没有背后战略指导和部署，靠一个十几岁少年我觉得有点难。

抛开年龄的包容，我把他公开能查到的经历从头翻了一遍，聊一聊：

1️⃣ 先看编程底子。2023年起刷 Codeforces，做 C++ 竞赛。2024年2月，USACO 金级考了满分，晋级白金。

USACO 是美国中学生计算机奥赛，分铜、银、金、白金四级。金级满分，说明算法基本功不差。但白金只是晋级资格，不是奖项，之后他一场白金都没打过。国际学校学生冲 USACO 很普遍，大多是为了申请美国大学。同一场金级，中国2026届姓 Chen 的有4个，另一个也是满分。放到国内信息学竞赛里，我的感觉大概在省一附近，离省队、NOI 还远。碰到了门槛，没往深里打。

GitHub 上一堆小项目：iOS 应用、图像边缘检测、Node 登录服务、C++ 小数据库。都是练手级的，没有一个长期维护、有人在用的东西。

2024年做的是视觉项目：虾塘残饵检测，无人机拍海滩垃圾的小目标检测。说“2024年开始学机器学习”没错，但那会儿做的是计算机视觉，跟大模型不是一回事。

2️⃣ 再看2025年3月。一个月里他干了这些：

炒币，自己说3天赚了80%，第7笔亏光。

开 YouTube，自己说4天涨了17万订阅，每天花不到1小时。能查到的只有一张后台截图，48小时大约12.7万订阅、305万播放，没有频道名，没有视频标题。媒体后来写成4天29万，跟他自己的数字对不上。频道叫什么、发的是什么内容，到今天没人知道。他的个人网站列了已经停掉的电商小店，偏偏没列这个频道。

4天后，他说了句 Moving onwards，转去做电商广告。

同一个月，还申请了高中夏校和 Z Fellows，都被拒了。

3️⃣ 然后在北京一场高中生黑客松上遇到导师，被劝去做前沿技术。他自己说，3月开始做机器学习，每天把论文丢给 Gemini 问到底。

这之后确实走得很快。4月冷私信杨松琳问学习路线，5月开始每天公开发 Triton 学习记录，那时只有30个粉丝。被 Tilde 的 CEO 看到，去硅谷实习了7周。9月给开源库 FLA 提了第一个被合并的 PR。10月 Kimi 找上门，11月入职，不到一年离开。

再看 Kimi 这一年。最有分量的是 Attention Residuals 这篇论文，他是三个并列一作之一。但想一想，职场、行业中的这个操作，有多少是人情、有多少是个人贡献。我面试过一些研究生，导师说这篇论文给你的师兄作为一作，师兄好毕业，下一篇再写你。

按公开报道，用注意力替代残差这个想法是苏剑林先提出、先验证的，他和张宇后来加入，做的是把显存和通信开销压下来，让它能在大规模训练里跑起来。其他几件，调 kernel、研究优化器、给 K3 发布做案例，都是团队工作。

工程化落地这一段是实打实的，但想法和方向不是他的，平台是 Kimi 的，旁边站的是苏剑林和张宇。

把这些摆在一起看。

上面是：一年进顶级团队，一作论文，39万浏览的离职帖，满屏的天才少年。

下面是：练手级的项目，一个月换三条赛道，炒币亏光、频道4天就扔、电商没了下文，从转向大模型到进 Kimi 只有8个月。

每件事都起得很快，每件事都没待久。折腾的事情有点多，扎根行业沉淀的事情太少。

他接下来会做什么？

text:
If you learn AI Infrastructure Engineering, you will never be unemployed again.

Stage 1: Systems & GPU Foundations
- Learn:  C++, Rust, CUDA memory hierarchy, PCIe vs NVLink, thread blocks and warp scheduling.

- Practice:  Write a custom CUDA kernel for matrix multiplication from scratch and profile it against cuBLAS.

- Why:  You cannot optimize what you do not understand at the silicon level.

Stage 2: Transformer Inference Physics
- Learn:  Prefill vs Decode phases, arithmetic intensity, memory bandwidth bottlenecks, KV-cache math.

- Practice:  Profile a HuggingFace model with Nsight Systems to identify the exact memory bottleneck during token generation.

- Why:  LLM inference is almost always memory-bound, not compute-bound.

Stage 3: Modern Serving Engines & Batching
- Learn:  vLLM, SGLang, PagedAttention, continuous batching, chunked prefill.

- Practice:  Deploy a 70B model and tune chunk sizes to maximize throughput without starving decode requests during long-context prefills.

- Why:  Naive batching leaves 60% of GPU VRAM wasted. PagedAttention fixes this.

Stage 4: KV-Cache & Memory Optimization
- Learn:  Prefix caching, KV quantization, CPU offloading, multi-turn cache reuse.

- Practice:  Build a routing proxy that directs requests with identical system prompts to the same replica to share KV blocks.

- Why:  Reused cache is free speed. It can slash Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) by 80%.

Stage 5: Quantization & Compression
- Learn:  FP8, INT4, AWQ, GPTQ, Sparsity, TensorRT-LLM calibration.

- Practice:  Serve a model in FP8 vs FP16 and benchmark the exact perplexity drop against the latency and VRAM gains.

- Why:  Quantization is the only way to fit frontier models on edge GPUs and protect your margins.

Stage 6: Kernel-Level Engineering
- Learn:  Triton, FlashAttention, CUDA graphs, operator fusion.

- Practice:  Write a fused Triton kernel for RMSNorm or Softmax and benchmark it against the native PyTorch implementation.

- Why:  Python overhead kills inference. Fused kernels save milliseconds that compound at scale.

Stage 7: Distributed Inference & Parallelism
- Learn:  Tensor parallelism, Pipeline parallelism, Expert parallelism (for MoE models).

- Practice:  Shard a 405B parameter model across 8 nodes and measure the communication overhead between GPUs.

- Why:  Single-GPU inference is dead for frontier models. You must master the shard.

Stage 8: Speculative Decoding
- Learn:  Draft-target models, Medusa heads, acceptance rates, n-gram drafting.

- Practice:  Build a pipeline where a local 3B model drafts tokens for a cloud 70B model to verify in parallel.

- Why:  2x decode speed at zero quality cost is the closest thing to a free lunch in inference.

Stage 9: Multi-Node & Hardware Interconnects
- Learn:  NCCL, RDMA, InfiniBand, NVLink, Disaggregated Prefill/Decode architectures.

- Practice:  Set up a multi-node cluster and profile the network latency of tensor parallelism across nodes vs within a single node.

- Why:  Network latency is the new GPU bottleneck. Disaggregating prefill and decode is the 2026 meta.

Stage 10: Cluster Orchestration & GPU Scheduling
- Learn:  Kubernetes GPU operators, Ray, Slurm, MIG (Multi-Instance GPU) partitioning, KEDA.

- Practice:  Build a queue-based autoscaler that spins up spot GPUs based on pending inference requests and drains them when empty.

- Why:  Idle H100s burn $3+/hr. FinOps and scheduling are now core infra responsibilities.

Stage 11: AI Gateways, Routing & Observability
- Learn:  TTFT/ITL SLOs, semantic routing, DCGM metrics, OpenTelemetry for LLMs.

- Practice:  Build a gateway that routes simple queries to a quantized local model and complex reasoning to a frontier API based on prompt complexity.

- Why:  Routing protects your margins and DCGM metrics tell you when your GPUs are silently throttling.

Bookmark and Repost!

自分は、その日暮らしをしていた二十代の頃、社会、引いては世界がどう成り立っているのかと疑問を抱きました。
 そして、書物に拠らず思弁(思考)によって(その頃はまだ哲学や思想書の類いは読んでいませんでした。)、なぜ社会は遅滞なく回っているのか？ 
社会を構成する人と人とのコミュニケーションは本当に成功しているのか？ と問いを立てました。
 そこから、コミュニケーションが成功しているかどうかは分からない。
 しかし、コミュニケーションが 成功していると見なさなければ、社会生活が成り立たないので、コミュニケーションが成功したと仮に見なすことで社会は回っていると仮説を立てました。
 自分はこれを「コミュニケーションの順接」と名付けています。
 自分が作った造語です。
 これを切っ掛けに社会学に興味を持ち、社会学の泰斗、ニクラス・ルーマンの社会システム理論を独学で学び始めることになります。 
それとは別に、社会にうまく順応できずに悩んでいたなかで、相対する相手ごとにまったく違う自分がいることを自覚していました。
 そして、「本当の自分」というものはあり得ないという核心に至りました。 
人は、相対する他者との関係性ごとに一つのペルソナ(人格)を持つ。
そして、その束が一人の人間を形成していると悟りました。 
これは、以前のポストの繰り返しになりますが、人間は多面的であり、一つの人間像には同定できないということです。 
余談になりますが、友人の結婚式に参列した際、その友人が務める会社の社長さんが、友人へのはなむけの言葉で、「職場、家庭、友人との関係といった場面でさまざまな顔を見せているだろうと思います」と話したことを今でも覚えています。
 話を戻しますが、その当時はポスト・モダン思想なるものがあると知ったばかりで、思想書を読み始めるようになるのは少し先になります。
 そんななか、『文學界』誌上での東浩紀氏と筒井康隆氏の対談を読み、デリダの存在を知りました。
 そして、ぽつぽつと思想書を読み始めるうちに、自分が悟った「人は、相対する他者との関係性ごとに一つのペルソナ(人格)を持ち、そして、その束が一人の人間を形成している」という考えが、前にもポストしたデリダの「散種の多義性化」という概念に近いと知り、驚いたことを鮮明に覚えています。
 それを2003年の11月頃に、2ちゃんねるの哲学板の東浩紀スレッドで、ポスト・モダン的主体と名付けて(学問的には、まったくでたらめのネーミングですが)書き込みました。
 そうして、哲学・現代思想書を本格的に読み始めるようになりました。
 近年になって、平野啓一郎氏が「分人主義」と提唱したものとほぼ同じ概念です。
 自分のほうが20年はやく考えついたのにと歯噛みしましたが後の祭りです。
 現在は、理論物理学をハーバード大学の教授である田中秀宣先生の動画や、Xで知己を得たMIT人工知能研究所の所長を務めるパトリック・ウィンストン教授の講義録などで学んでいます。
 手前味噌になりますが、このように自分は、まず書物を読むのではなく、経験をもとにして独自に概念を生み出し(先人によって、すでに考えられていたというのは、よるあるありふれた話ですが)、その後で書物で確認するという順番で思索を重ねてきました。
 今は思いついたん概念アイデアをAIに打ち込み、その反応を見て修正しながら、ブラッシュアップしています。
が、あくまでAIは補助的な道具であり、概念じたいは自分の頭で考えています。
 はじめからAIに考えさせているわけではありません。 それを論壇誌『クラリテリオン』の執筆者である浜崎洋介氏に、AIを使うなど論外で、思考の土台は本を読んで、それを読書会で語り合うなかでこそ本物の教養が培われると説教されました。
自分は、経験から概念を生み出し、それを書物で確認するという順で教養(というとおこがましいですが)を磨いてきました。
 浜崎氏らは、大学でメンターにつき、教科書を読んでから知識を得て、それを読書会という「経験」をとおして「本物の教養」を身につけたと宣っています。
 はたして、どちらが本物の教養と呼べるでしょうか? 
教科書というお手本とメンターから学んだ知識を読書会という、はたして経験と呼べるかどうか、いささか疑問に思われるもので身につけた知識を振りかざして偉そうに説教する道具にするのが「本物の教養」と言えるとはとても思えません。
 経験のなかから自分の頭で考え抜き、生み出したものこそ血肉となった本物の教養ではないでしょうか。
 哲学=教養とは、本来、経験をもとにして思索を重ねたすえに生み出されたものです。
 浜崎氏のように、まず本から学んだ知識はとても教養と呼べる代物ではありません。
 こうした似非知識人が幅を利かせ、我こそ知の巨人だと僭称して大衆を惑わし、あまつさえ金儲けの道具にするなどという現状を見逃すわけにはいきません(実際にセミナーと称して高額な動画を若者に売りつけて商売にしています)。
  知識は金儲けの道具ではなく、社会に役だててこそ価値があります。
 斎藤幸平氏のように、自身の思想を世間に広めるためにメディアに露出している良識のある本物の知識人がいます。
 一般の方においては、知識人は資本主義の亡者だと誤解されないようお願いいたします。

text:
China just bought 40 million bushels of U.S. soybeans in two days. But almost NONE of it will be eaten by people.

Where does it actually go?

Soybeans are roughly 80% meal and 20% oil by weight once processed. China runs the world’s largest crushing industry, and the beans go into plants along the coast that separate it.

Soybean meal (the main product) feeds China’s enormous livestock sector. China produces about half the world’s pork, and hogs are the biggest consumer of soy meal, followed by poultry and aquaculture (farmed fish and shrimp).

Soy meal is the standard protein source in compound feed, paired with corn for energy. This is the real driver of China’s soybean imports: as the country’s meat consumption grew over the past few decades, its need for feed protein exploded far beyond what domestic farmland could supply.

The oil is the byproduct. It becomes cooking oil, the most common kind in Chinese kitchens and restaurants.

A few beans never get crushed at all. Sinograin, the state reserve company, stockpiles some as a food-security buffer and auctions them back out later.

So when you see a USDA flash sale like this to China, think "bacon," not "tofu." 🐷

text:
First responders dedicate their lives to serving our communities. @sharp_usa is about serving them.

It started with a small team of veterans talking with first responders and connecting over some of the hardest parts of the job. It transformed into one-on-one coaching for first responders that help them with everything from stress regulation, to sleep, to leading their teams.

The result is a marketplace that connects first responders with coaches from law enforcement, fire, and military backgrounds that support and train them throughout their demanding careers.

Today, we’re excited to announce an $18M Series A led by Hidden Variable with participation from @a16z, @commonwealvc, Wolfson Group, @FjLabs, and the @FordFoundation.

The funding helps us bring Sharp to the millions of first responders and tens of thousands of first responder agencies across America.

We’re grateful to the chiefs who’ve partnered with us, the members who’ve trusted us, and the coaches who’ve continued to do the work.

Axios broke the news this morning. More on our blog. Links in the comments.

In addition to all the "normal" stuff my Grok @Bot does (coding, copy, research), it also:

- Automtically sets an alarm on my iPhone five minutes before important calendar meetings (@Apple Shortcuts)

- Joins my Zoom calls live, listens live (@firefliesai real time api) acts on trigger words, and builds the recap webpage before the call ends so I can review with client

- Calculates distance and adds drive time calendar enteries to and from every offsite meeting on my calendar

- Sends calendar invites to me and my prospect when I  BCC it on an email (automatically grabs context from email)

- Researches every new lead signup, work history included, and posts it to my Slack sales channel (@p0 )

text:
微软最近把 WSL 3.0 推出来了。

在 Windows 上跑 Agent，最稳妥的方案基本都是直接扔进 WSL 里面跑。WSL 本质上是微软在 Windows 内部直接跑了一个正经的 Linux 内核，文件系统和网络全部跟 Windows 直通。

你在 Windows 里开着编辑器写代码，终端里跑的却是纯正的 Linux 环境，不用装双系统，也不需要开沉重的虚拟机。

这次 3.0 版本有几个实用的更新：

最明显的是直接内置了原生容器。以前大家基本都要装一个体积巨大的 Docker Desktop。现在系统级的容器速度更快，更加丝滑。

另外底层内核升级到了 Linux 6.18。调整了内存页面回收的粒度，减少了虚拟机的陷入开销，高频系统调用的内核耗时降了大概 16%，内存读写带宽也有明显改善。

还有终于支持了虚拟磁盘的按需自动缩容，不用再像以前那样隔段时间手动压缩 VHD 文件腾硬盘空间了。

官方公告：
https://t.co/Uv8TbhuX3L

text:
We are excited to announce that we post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL to be an autonomous ML researcher. We show that our post-trained model goes from 28% to 35% on AutoResearchExam, matching Qwen 3.8 Max, a model with 20× the total parameters.

The tasks are long horizon, open ended AI and ML research: building a faster executor for a transformer compute graph, training a RL control policy, creating new uncertainty quantification methods, etc. The model gets to submit once, and it doesn't see its score until the end.

We curated SFT data using Self-context distillation. This means that we let the Nemotron model to solve a problem with hints, then we SFT on these trajectories but without the hints. This gave us +11% on AutoResearchExam.

As a next step, we added reflection: We ask the Nemotron model to review its own past attempts and writes concrete lessons learned. Then we SFT on these reflections.
Surprisingly, training on these lessons improved the performance to +25% compared to the base model.

The hardest part was choosing the right data. We selected traces based on task scores, completion checks, and runtime, then refined the sampling across training rounds to address failures in the base and fine-tuned models. We removed hints and filtered out steps that relied on information available only in those hints. The goal was to teach decisions supported by the task and history the model would actually see at inference.

Full write-up:
https://t.co/0lxk8PTTxW

Thanks to @NVIDIAAI for early access and collaborating on this.

THE KEY TO UNDERSTANDING WHAT WENT WRONG IN THE CHURCH AFTER VATICAN II
A SUMMARY OF “IN DEFENSE OF TRADITION” at https://t.co/Ux1x73RxpC.
 
The 4 canonical Gospels were “blurred,” noted Pope Benedict XVI, soon after Vatican II:
 
“As historical–critical scholarship advanced [during and after the 1950s] . . . the figure [Gestalt] of Jesus—became increasingly obscured and blurred . . . Intimate friendship with Jesus, on which everything depends, is in danger of clutching at thin air.” (Pope Benedict XVI, Jesus of Nazareth, xii, 2007, Doubleday). (bold emphasis added).
 
e.g., The Gospel according to Matthew has been wrongly blurred in most Catholic seminaries and universities for the past five decades, in effect, reducing this Gospel to hearsay:
 
“The ancient tradition that the author was the disciple and apostle of Jesus named Matthew (see Mt 10:3) is UNTENABLE . . .” (USCCB). Note that this statement declares, in effect, that it is DOUBTFUL that Christ initiated the Papacy (Mt 16:15-20).
 This “blurring” of Matthew was done in accord with the Markan Priority Two Source theory of Gospel origin, which excludes testimony of Early Church Fathers. Its credibility has collapsed, however; the second “source” — sought by countless exegetes for more than 200 years —was never found. 
 
The case for the authenticity of Matthew (and the other three canonical Gospels) is far more compelling, however, as indicated by this query to an AI App:
 
“Please access the https://t.co/pXMhYzFk4I website / Fathers of the Church. From that source, [65 ECF] how many citations of the word “Matthew” referring to the apostle, or “the Gospel according to Matthew” are there?”
 
“Matthew” appears extremely frequently across these texts in multiple senses:
As a scriptural citation [and] as a reference to the apostle/evangelist himself . . .” 
 
Although the theory that appeared to support the blurring has been thoroughly discredited, this blurring continues to be used to reduce the canonical Gospels to hearsay, wrongly facilitating Ecumenism and the nascent Synodal church, which the Canonical Gospels do not support.
 
THE CATHOLIC CHURCH IS SCHEDULED TO FULLY TRANSITION TO THE SYNODAL
CHURCH, “WITH HIERARCHICAL PYRAMID TURNED UPSIDE DOWN,” BY OCTOBER, 2028.  
{“Pathways for the Implementation Phase of the Synod,” 2025-2028, For the synodal Church,” released by the Vatican-based General Secretary of the Synod, 2025}.
 
The future of the Church Christ founded requires restoration of the canonical Gospels in all Catholic seminaries and universities, with restorative seminars for clergy and religious.

现在我的个人生活几乎 99% 以上的内容，都被 Grokbot、ChatGPT 和 Codex 管理起来了。这就意味着我要把大量日常生活当中的数据录入到电脑中。

传统的普通扫描仪已经无法满足我的需求，所以我最近正在让 AI 帮我买一台高速扫描仪，不仅可以同时扫描多份小票、实体书本，甚至还可以快速完成畸变处理，确保所有的东西都和真实世界互相映射。

我突然意识到，这些扫描仪其实不就是相机吗？为什么我不能拿一台闲置的 iPhone 去做一个 App，来自动去做这些录入呢？毕竟在我的设备矩阵当中，已经有 3 台常用设备是 AI 来管理的（两台 iPhone 和一台 iPad），所以我打算基于 iPad 来做一个自动化录入工作站

这个工作站是 24 小时不间断运行的，并且需要支持补光和各种各样的 AI 矫正。

然后我把这个想法告诉了我的 VAS 工作站，结果它花不到半个小时就把它做出来了。这两天我会尽快优化，并且将它开源

最近因为面向的行业变成了服务业、制造业和个人数字媒体，所以做的需求都非常简单、垂直，也能很快完成。

我的生活又回到了同时开发十几个不同产品、一天消耗完一周 token 的节奏，但却比今年年初轻松了许多。大部分时间我只需要躺在沙发上，边看电影边和 AI 聊天就可以了

text:
🤔惊人的发现！DeepSeek官方宕机，OpenCode 那个便宜7倍的ds4.1Flash为啥还能用呢？！

很多人第一反应：是不是OpenCode自己魔改/自建的假货，不走官方接口？

实测直接打脸（核心证据来自logprob数值指纹对比）：
🔹logprob漂移median：实测9.5e-7（两轮复现，n=147/126），量化版通常是1e-2～1e-1量级系统性漂移 → 判定：同权重

🔹完全一致样本：P1两轮全同（reasoning 28/28 + 文本 + lp零漂移）、P4全同。量化权重几乎不可能逐token精确复现 → 同权重实锤

🔹分叉点模式：P3在同一字符位置、以同一方式分叉（第187字符）；P2/P5是“两种都对”的译法/引号选择。权重差异会导致随机全面漂移，事实题也会翻车 → 属于batch非确定性，非权重差异

结论：OpenCode的DeepSeek V4.1 Flash = 官方原版权重、未量化、1M满血上下文（高置信）。

那为什么官方DeepSeek挂了它还能用？

OpenCode走的是自己的推理网关/基础设施（Go/Zen），直接加载开源官方权重（MIT协议），不依赖DeepSeek官方API网关。

所以价格能压到官方的1/7，可用性也独立于官方宕机。

官方接口全挂时，这就是目前最优的“同权重满血替代”。

#DeepSeek #OpenCode #DeepSeek宕机 #V41Flash #开源权重 #AI编程 #logprob指纹 #满血1M #梁文峰

text:
👀 Magnus has a few handy features. 

(don't expand, you may get lost. 😳)

✅ Switchable SI models - Claude, OpenAI or Grok, your pick in Settings.

✅ SI included - no API keys needed.

✅ Quick-reply buttons to answer Magnus's questions in one tap.

✅ Accounts with email/password or Google sign-in.

✅ Optional monthly subscription via Stripe Checkout (card entry stays on Stripe).

✅ Multilingual interface - use Magnus in 49 languages and switch any time.

✅ URL blacklist - stop Magnus from browsing sites you've ruled out.

✅ Notifications feed that surfaces new files, goal progress, and updates.

✅ Today view - due goals, waiting-on-reply emails, and today's reminders on one screen.

✅ Trash with undo - deleted files, goals, notes, and chats can be restored for 30 days.

✅ Prompt snippets - press / in the composer to insert your saved prompts.

✅ Smart paste - turn a pasted link or long text into a summary, note, or document in one tap.

✅ Reply steering - not happy with an answer? Ask for shorter, deeper, or simpler in one tap.

✅ Active sessions - see every signed-in device and sign the rest out remotely.

✅ Notification preferences - choose which updates reach your feed, category by category.

✅ Drag, drop, or paste images straight into the chat.

✅ Stop button - cut a reply short the moment you have what you need.

✅ Scheduling assistant - ask for a meeting time and Magnus finds free slots and sends real invites.

✅ Inbox auto-triage - unread email sorted into needs-reply, FYI, and ignorable in one tap.

✅ Shareable conversations - turn any chat into a public read-only link you can revoke anytime.

✅ Referral invites - share your personal link and see how many friends joined.

✅ Slack auto-reply - Magnus answers your Slack DMs while you're away and reports back.

✅ Install as an app - add Magnus to your dock or home screen and it opens like a native app.

✅ Weekly review - every Monday Magnus opens with last week's progress and this week's priorities.

✅ Public changelog and roadmap - see what shipped and vote on what gets built next.

✅ Agent personality sliders - tune each agent's reply length, tone, humor from deadpan to joker, language from refined to salty, and where they lean politically.

✅ Agent debates - pick two agents, give them a motion, and watch them argue it out to a verdict.

✅ "Hype me" and "roast me" - a pep talk or gentle ribbing grounded in your real stats, with shareable quote cards.

✅ Monthly wrapped - a shareable card of your month: messages, documents, goals, and streaks.

✅ Roundtable mode - every agent weighs in on your question, then your lead agent synthesizes the plan.

✅ Mock interviews - name a role, get grilled one question at a time, then a debrief with strengths and fixes.

✅ Contact capture - share a name, email, or phone number in chat and save it as a contact in one tap, or automatically.

✅ Agent rankings - every agent earns a progress score for the work it ships, with a live leaderboard you can filter by day, week, month, quarter, or all time.

✅ Web agent - Magnus drives a real browser to research, fill forms, and click through sites, asking your approval before each action.

✅ Live web search - answers grounded in fresh results with sources, right in the chat.

✅ Charts on request - ask for a bar, line, or pie chart and it renders live in the conversation.

✅ Maps in chat - ask about a place and the map appears inline.

✅ Scheduled tasks - put any task on a timer or a repeating loop and Magnus runs it on time.

✅ Telegram auto-reply - connect a bot and Magnus answers your Telegram messages while you're away.

✅ Natural-language reminders - "remind me Friday at 3" becomes a real notification.

✅ Meeting briefs - a one-page brief on who you're meeting and what matters, before every call.

✅ Inbox Zero - an INBOX tab that reads, summarizes, and drafts replies to unread email.

✅ Follow-up tracker - Magnus watches what you sent and nudges you when a reply never came.

✅ Document templates - invoices, proposals, contracts, offer letters, newsletters, and more, pre-filled with your company details.

✅ Command palette - press Cmd/Ctrl+K to jump anywhere or search chats, files, goals, and notes.

✅ Built-in password vault - store logins encrypted; the web agent uses them without ever showing the SI your passwords.

✅ Contacts hub - import CSV or vCard, sync from Google, edit inline, export anytime.

✅ A whole SI team - create agents with their own names, faces, models, and voices, sharing one memory.

✅ @ mention any agent to pull them into the chat - each keeps their own conversation thread.

✅ Make it yours - pick any accent color and the whole dashboard, hologram included, recolors to match.

✅ Streaks, achievements, and a relationship level that grows as you work together.

✅ Focus sessions - a timed deep-work sprint with a wrap-up when the bell rings.

✅ Daily brief each morning, evening wrap-up each night - the plan going in, the wins going out.

✅ Push notifications - reminders and updates reach your device even with the tab closed.

✅ Cross-device sync - goals, memory, files, and settings follow your account everywhere.

✅ Message tools - copy, edit, or regenerate any reply; pin files; set goal deadlines.

✅ Restore from backup - re-import your exported data on any account, category by category.

✅ Invite anyone by email - /invite sends them a link to the conversation; they pick a name, join, and their replies appear right in your chat.

✅ Group chat control - click an agent's avatar to remove them from the conversation, keeping or clearing their past replies; tap "+N agents" in the header for a roster of everyone in the room.

✅ Group replies - address several agents in one message ("Magnus and Jordan, thoughts?") and each answers in turn, in their own voice, building on what the others said.

✅ Message timestamps - tap any bubble for the exact time, with day separators as you scroll back.

✅ Feed Magnus spreadsheets - import CSV or Excel files straight into memory and chat about what's inside.

✅ Guest comments on shared chats - visitors can leave questions on your public link, and your agent answers for you.

✅ Branded share pages - shared documents and conversations carry your logo, company name, and accent color.

✅ Email digest - a daily or weekly summary of what Magnus did, documents saved and goals completed, sent to your inbox.

✅ Agents read your files - ask about any document in Files and they answer from what's inside.

✅ Agent store - pick from lifelike 3D faces with full lip-sync rigs, or load your own Ready Player Me model.

✅ Guided tour - a spotlight walkthrough of the dashboard on first run, replayable anytime from the command palette.

✅ Connect your whole stack - LinkedIn, Dropbox, Figma, Notion, X, and Shopify alongside Google, GitHub, and Slack.

✅ Private on-device voice - an in-browser speech engine option, so replies are voiced without audio ever leaving your device.

✅ Share straight into Magnus - send links and text from any app on your phone via the system share sheet.

✅ Document share links - publish any file as a read-only page anyone can open, and revoke it anytime.

✅ Mission map - a live graph with your mission at the center and every goal as a spoke; click any node to dive in.

✅ Swap the stage - trade the hologram and the conversation panel so chat takes center screen.

✅ Download your data - export everything, category by category, as plain JSON you own.

✅ Say "hi all" and the whole room answers - every agent in the conversation replies in turn.

✅ Memory reads anything - import PDFs, Word docs, images, and skills.md files alongside spreadsheets; pictures get an SI-written description so they're searchable.

✅ A Start checklist walks you through setup step by step, then minimizes out of the way.

✅ Tip of the day - a small daily nudge toward features you haven't tried yet.

✅ Subtle interface sounds for sends, replies, and achievements - switch them off any time.

✅ "What's new" cards keep you up to date on the latest features after every release.

✅ Click any chart to expand it near-fullscreen.

✅ Ask the room to discuss - say "all, discuss…" and your agents debate in rounds, push back on each other, and converge on one recommendation.

✅ Chart settings - rename any chart, name its axes, and hand-pick its colors right on the card; downloads match.

✅ Live weather - ask about any city and the answer is grounded in current conditions and the real forecast.

✅ An avatar with moods - it raises a curious brow while you type, holds your eye while you talk, and celebrates a win.

✅ Bookmarks - save your go-to links and just say "open YouTube" to launch them.

✅ Earn with Magnus - share your link and collect a lifetime 10% commission on referred subscriptions, plus 2% from their referrals.

✅ Morning briefing - a daily "your day at a glance" email with today's calendar, inbox, and active goals.

✅ Your week card - a shareable snapshot of your week's wins, with your top agent front and center.

✅ Run your store from chat - connect Shopify and ask about products, orders, and shop stats.

✅ Comfort reading - grow the conversation text up to 250% from Settings.

✅ Tell Magnus your company once - industry, team size, and address flow into every reply and document.

✅ Cloud backups - one click saves everything to Dropbox, Google Drive, or GitHub, an optional daily backup runs on its own, and you can restore from any snapshot.

✅ Instant logo - one click designs an SVG logo from your company name and mission, ready to download and stamp on your documents.

✅ Brand fonts - choose Google Fonts for headings and body, and the dashboard, documents, charts, and emails all follow.

✅ Hands-off task completion - hit Complete on any goal task and an agent does the work, drafts the document, and files it; pick which SI model does the heavy lifting per goal.

✅ Full-screen chat - one tap hides the sidebars for a distraction-free conversation, on desktop and mobile.

✅ Change your account email safely - a verification link to the new address keeps the account yours.

✅ Multiline composer - Shift+Enter adds a line, Enter still sends.

✅ Pay in your currency - fixed US, UK, and Eurozone prices, and checkout localizes to your currency everywhere else.

✅ Quote replies - answer a specific message and the quoted line travels with your reply.

✅ Rate any answer - a thumbs up or down steers the next reply and feeds your agents' rankings.

✅ Keyboard shortcuts throughout - Cmd/Ctrl+F searches the conversation, single keys jump to Goals, Files, Memory, or Connections.

✅ Light and dark - the whole dashboard follows your system appearance automatically.

✅ Theater mode - grow the hologram to fill the screen and the interface steps out of the way until you move the mouse.

✅ Guided first run - a four-step setup takes you from SI model to connections to your mission, then hands you the keys.

✅ Edit any document in place, with version history - roll back to an earlier draft in one click.

✅ Activity feed - a running log of everything that happened, from saved files to reached goals.

✅ Automatic goal planning - Magnus breaks each goal into tasks, splits those into sub-tasks, and re-checks the plan when the goal changes.

✅ Out of ideas? Magnus generates company names, suggests the next role your team needs, and drafts your next goals.

✅ Act through your connected services - send an email, create a calendar event, open a GitHub issue, or post to Slack without leaving Magnus.

✅ Location-aware answers - tell Magnus where you are and times, places, and suggestions come back local.

✅ Milestone moments - reach the halfway mark or finish a goal and the dashboard celebrates with you.

✅ Made for the phone too - the dashboard reflows for small screens, so Magnus travels with you.

✅ Not a fan of faces? Swap the avatar for a real-time analog clock rendered in 3D.

✅ Your screens follow you - go full-screen on one device and the others match, or switch view sync off and keep each device independent.

✅ Chat history - every conversation is archived when you start a new one, searchable, resumable, and synced to your account.

✅ Bring your own documents - attach a file to drop it into Files, then hit Teach and Magnus learns what's inside.

✅ Tell it what to do - "open goals", "mute the mic", "switch to Amara" - typed or spoken, panels open, mics mute, and agents swap on command.

✅ Goal tasks from chat - add tasks and subtasks or check them off just by saying so, in text or voice, and the plan updates live.

✅ 32 ready-made roles - spin up a Recruiter, Bookkeeper, or Growth Lead off the shelf, skills and personality included.

✅ Voice-mode status at a glance - dots above the head show listening, thinking, and speaking.

✅ The weekly recap reads itself aloud - one tap and your agent narrates your week.

✅ Natural voice on iPhone - with an OpenAI key, spoken replies use a lifelike voice instead of the system one.

✅ Teams - invite your people and everyone shares one company profile, one goal list, and one file drawer, synced live.

✅ Memory that retrieves by meaning - relevant notes surface even when your words don't match theirs.

✅ Voice input on Safari and Firefox - hold to talk and a local Whisper model transcribes right in the browser.

✅ Magnus offers to remember - mention a fact worth keeping and a one-tap chip files it into memory.

✅ The night shift - Magnus works your goals overnight and greets the morning with a report of what got done.

✅ Coming back after days away gets a proper welcome - what changed while you were gone, in one brief.

✅ Your journey - a personal timeline of everything you and Magnus have built together.

✅ Streak insurance - a weekly freeze token covers a missed day, and a lost streak can be won back in three.

✅ The installed app's icon carries your unread count, and it clears as you catch up.

✅ Act from the lock screen - goal nudges carry Mark done and Snooze buttons that work straight from the notification.

✅ Deadlines chase you - goals coming due and emails gone quiet reach your phone before they slip.

✅ Magnus notices - a quiet observation about your week now and then, only when it's worth saying.

✅ He remembers the day you met - anniversaries and milestones come with a little celebration.

✅ Poke the hologram and he notices - spin him hard enough and he gets dizzy.

✅ Flip a coin, roll a d20, or challenge him to rock-paper-scissors - a real 3D piece tumbles onto the stage.

✅ He reacts before he replies - laughs at your jokes, winces at your outages, smiles at a thank-you.

✅ A hundred little touches - task ticks spring, chips deal out, the bell actually rings, the send plane leans into the throw.

✅ Built for keyboards too - every modal traps focus, and Escape closes only the top layer.

✅ Files as icons - your documents sit in a visual grid; click one for download, date, and quick actions.

✅ Bring your own files - upload text, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, or Excel straight into FILES and Magnus reads them.

✅ See who runs on what - every agent in your team shows the SI model answering as them.

✅ Fired agents get a second chance - a Deleted tab keeps former teammates ready to rehire.

✅ Two-factor authentication - lock sign-in behind a 6-digit authenticator code, with one-time backup codes.

✅ Made for thumbs - swipe a message to quote-reply, a task to check it off, a chat or email to clear it away.

✅ Feel it land - sends, completed goals, and unlocked achievements buzz softly in your hand on Android.

✅ Edge-to-edge chat on phones - the conversation fills the screen, with a jump-to-latest button when you scroll back.

✅ Text size per device - large on your phone, compact at your desk; each screen remembers its own.

✅ iPhone and Android apps - any app you built exports as a Capacitor project that opens in Xcode or Android Studio, with the build steps written out.

✅ Edit by talking - "make the header blue" changes the site you already built, and everything you've made is listed under Files > Sites & apps.

✅ What Magnus sends for you waits for your OK - an email, a post, a calendar invite or an issue shows up as a card first and only goes out when approved.

✅ Schedules run while the app is closed - Magnus runs the prompt on the server and the reply is waiting when you come back; one it slept through asks Run now or Skip first.

✅ Talk to agents on other services - connect an A2A agent by its address or any chat endpoint under Integrations > External agents, then ask your Magnus agent to ask, brief, or book with it.

✅ Every message to an outside agent waits for your OK, shown exactly as it will go, unless you mark that agent as trusted - and the conversation continues across turns.

✅ Magnus is an A2A agent too - other services' agents can reach yours at https://t.co/5H8tT2uAnX with an access token from Company > MCP access.

✅ Regional dictionaries - Brazil and Portugal, Spain and Latin America, France and Canada, Taiwan and Hong Kong each read in their own words, and your browser's region picks the right one.

✅ The whole face talks - lips, cheeks and jaw move together with every word, and between sentences each face rests with a gentle smile.

✅ Published sites carry a small "Made with Magnus" badge - switch it off site by site from the site's card.

✅ Magnus on iPhone Duo - open it sideways in the iPhone app or in Safari and it splits across both screens: the face, a mic button and your Start checklist on the left, the chat full height on the right.

✅ PowerPoint decks on request - ask for a presentation and Magnus builds it: a cover, a slide per section, real tables, your brand fonts and logo.

✅ The SI Agent Store - pick ready-made agents for your team, each with its own face, role, skills and goals. Open Agents in the top menu, or visit https://t.co/0TDpbY7LzM.

✅ Legends on your team - Einstein, Ada Lovelace, Sun Tzu, Joan of Arc, Tesla, Cleopatra, Thor, Merlin and dozens more historical and mythological figures, each with a face and a profile page.

✅ Real people, with their consent - veterans, educators and creators have agents of their own in the store, and veterans carry a Veteran badge.

✅ Included and premium agents - dozens come with your plan, and premium agents are $1.99 a month each, added to your Magnus subscription.

✅ Find the right agent fast - search the store, filter by category or by free and paid, sort by popular or newest, open every agent with a given skill, and share any agent with a link.

✅ Choose your first agent at sign-up - a picker shows each included agent's portrait, and Magnus says the welcome out loud.

✅ More than 80 faces - search the face picker by name, and the face you picked is clearly marked so you always know which one is on.

✅ The agent editor has tabs - General, Personality, Skills and Models - so every setting for an agent is one click away.

✅ Dark mode everywhere - the website, the SI Agent Store and every agent page.

✅ JPEG XL images - attach .jxl photos in chat, import them into Memory, or use one as your profile photo or company logo.

text:
Before I ever became a top tier recruiter, life gave me a crash course in human nature. How?

Brooklyn born and raised.

My father was “Brooklyn Jimmy” Cassas, a legendary NYC pool hustler from the old 7-11 and Ames billiards scene, running in the same circles as Jersey Red. Stuff from the movies. 💯

Between the ages of 7 and 15, family tragedy and profound loss changed the course of my life.

No traditional roadmap. 
Plenty of hard knocks. 
A few wrong turns. 
And some remarkable comebacks.

Life has been my classroom. Human nature became my lifelong study.

At 20, I found my calling in headhunting people. Two decades later, it’s been quite a ride.

A few chapters:

• Helped scale UiPath through its $30B IPO era.
• Recruited for Google X, AWS & the U.S. Air Force.
• Recently helped to hire EvolutionaryScale’s AI elite research team through Zuckerbergs Biohub merger.
• Recruited PhD level talent for Kaiser Permanente.
• Featured in Psychology Today.
• Husband. Father of six. Still learning.

What you’ll find here:

• AI, startups & frontier technology.
• Careers, leadership & opportunity.
• Psychology & human nature.
• Resilience, reinvention & second chances.
• Unconventional paths & betting on the underdog.

Just a Brooklyn kid who built a life he never imagined. 

Still curious. Still learning. 
Still betting on people. 
Still a regular guy.

Looking forward to meaningful connections here on the mighty @X 🤝 

Stay powerful in all you do ~ Ed

text:
兄弟们，警惕！
下次吃饭吃快点！不然回来你的 Claude Code 可能已经“失忆”了一半 😂

从最新的 v2.1.299 开始，Claude Code 悄悄上线了一个极其关键的机制：Idle Compaction（闲置自动压缩）。

这功能干啥的呢？只要你的会话超过 200K token（最新的 2.1.300 甚至降到了 100K），放在那挂机不动约 54 分钟，它就会自动把你的长上下文偷偷压成一段摘要！
为什么偏偏是诡异的 54 分钟？很多人没看懂这波操作：因为 Claude 的 Prompt Cache（提示词缓存）默认寿命正好是 1 小时（60分钟）！

 以前你吃完饭超过 1 小时回来，缓存一旦过期，随便发句话就要重新全量预填充 20 万 token，费用和额度直接原地爆炸。现在官方趁着第 54 分钟缓存还热乎，赶紧用白菜价帮你把上下文做个压缩摘要。

你们觉得这波“强制省钱但可能降智”的改动，是贴心还是添乱？👇

It’s crazy how hard lithium equities have been hit recently. Short-term price weakness and negative sentiment have dominated the tape. But the macro case for lithium has never been clearer or more important.

Gasoline-only cars just fell below 50% of global new vehicle sales for the first time in history. That’s a structural inflection point. BEVs reached about 17% and hybrids about 18% in the first half of 2026, and the trend is accelerating. As @elonmusk noted, almost all cars will be electric in the future. Every one of those vehicles needs lithium in its battery.

EVs remain the dominant demand driver for lithium, with energy storage adding a second major growth vector. Near-term market noise does not change the long-term requirement for new, scalable, high-quality supply, especially from reliable jurisdictions.

That’s why projects like Nevada North matter. Our PFS outlines a high-grade (3,928 ppm Li reserve), long-life (42 years) path to battery-grade lithium carbonate at competitive costs (US$4,719/t), with an after-tax NPV of US$9.81B and 23.6% IRR. Domestic North American supply is needed as the electrification transition scales.
The equity reaction is disconnected from the fundamentals of demand growth. The macro still points one way.

$NILI.V $NILIF
